title: Build a Validated Kubernetes Runtime for NVIDIA Dynamo | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's AI Cluster Runtime (AICR), part of the DSX AI Factory Platform, packages the Dynamo distributed inference framework and its Kubernetes dependencies (GPU Operator, DRA, KAI Scheduler, Grove, NVSentinel, Prometheus, agentgateway) into validated recipes with pinned versions, deployed in a five-step snapshot-recipe-bundle-deploy-validate flow. Dynamo 1.4.2 drops NATS by default, uses TCP for requests and ZMQ for KV-cache events, and supports KV-cache-aware routing through either its own Frontend router or the Gateway API Inference Extension/EPP path. A native Rust EPP is coming in Dynamo 1.5.

themes.theme: Why inference needs a validated runtime layer

insights.claim: Deploying NVIDIA Dynamo on Kubernetes is only a first step. A working model deployment also needs GPU drivers, resource allocation, scheduling, networking and monitoring to work together, and resolving these dependencies takes time away from testing models and applications.
insights.so_what: Infrastructure integration, not the serving engine, is a major friction point in production AI inference.
insights.quote: A successful model deployment requires more: GPU drivers, resource allocation, scheduling, networking, and monitoring must all work together.

insights.claim: NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR), part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, packages Dynamo and its supporting infrastructure into validated recipes, each defining a configuration for a specific environment and workload with pinned component versions, compatibility constraints and validation checks.
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is extending its control from GPUs up into the Kubernetes cluster software layer for AI factories.

insights.claim: A DynamoGraphDeployment specifies how vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT LLM run in pods. Below it, a production cluster needs the right GPU Operator driver stack, discoverable GPU nodes, a DRA driver, topology-aware gang scheduling, node health signals, Prometheus metrics and, optionally, a Gateway API/EPP ingress path.
insights.so_what: This checklist shows how many layers of the stack NVIDIA now ships for inference clusters.
insights.quote: But the graph is only the top of the stack. A production inference cluster also needs a runtime layer below it.

themes.theme: What the AICR Dynamo recipe ships

insights.claim: AICR ships version 1.4.2 of the dynamo-platform chart with the Dynamo operator, runtime images and the nvidia.com/v1beta1 DynamoGraphDeployment CRD, where v1beta1 replaces the former v1alpha1 API.
insights.so_what: Promotion of the API to beta signals Dynamo is maturing toward production stability.
insights.quote: v1beta1 replaces the former v1alpha1 API version.
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: The recipe maps each runtime prerequisite to a component: NVIDIA GPU Operator, Node Feature Discovery, the DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs, KAI Scheduler for gang scheduling, Grove for multi-component serving graphs, NVSentinel and Nodewright for node health, a Prometheus stack and agentgateway for ingress. It also pins versions and records selectors, tolerations and checksums.
insights.so_what: A large share of the inference cluster stack is NVIDIA-authored open-source components.
insights.quote: the recipe pins component versions and records configuration values, node selectors, tolerations, checksums, and validation expectations to make deployment reproducible
insights.locator: In addition, the recipe pins component
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: In Dynamo 1.4, frontends, workers, GAIE/EPP components and other services discover each other through Kubernetes resources, so AICR's default path no longer uses NATS and the dynamo-platform chart no longer installs it by default. NATS remains available as an opt-in.
insights.so_what: Dropping an extra messaging dependency simplifies Kubernetes-native Dynamo deployments.
insights.quote: AICR’s default path therefore no longer uses NATS, and the dynamo-platform chart no longer installs it by default.
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: For the Amazon EKS Dynamo inference recipe on GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 systems, AICR v1.0.0 selects tested chart versions including GPU Operator v26.7.1, NVIDIA DRA GPU Driver 0.5.0, KAI Scheduler v0.16.9, Grove v0.1.0-alpha.13, Dynamo Platform 1.4.2 and Agent Gateway v1.5.0.
insights.so_what: A first validated recipe targets NVL72 rack-scale systems on AWS, the flagship cloud deployment for NVIDIA inference.

insights.claim: Agentic workloads repeatedly extend long token prefixes such as system prompts, tool definitions, conversation history and tool results. If a turn lands on a worker without that prefix in GPU memory, the system reprocesses tokens, so Dynamo routes requests to workers that already hold the relevant KV blocks.
insights.so_what: Cache-aware routing becomes a key efficiency lever as agentic workloads grow, which raises the value of inference orchestration software.
insights.quote: If a turn reaches a worker without that prefix in GPU memory, the system reprocesses intermediate tokens instead of reusing cached results.
insights.locator: Agentic workloads repeatedly extend long token
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: Dynamo can separate prefill from decode (disaggregated serving), which have different GPU, memory, latency and batching characteristics. Cache-miss rates depend on the workload, with long agentic sessions behaving differently from one-off chats, so operators can scale prefill and decode capacity independently.
insights.so_what: Independent scaling of prefill and decode lets operators match GPU spend to request mix.
insights.quote: Disaggregated serving enables operators to scale and tune prefill and decode capacity independently for a given request mix.
insights.locator: Dynamo can also separate prompt processing
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: In Dynamo 1.4.2 the request plane and KV-cache event plane are separate: the default AICR path uses TCP for requests and ZMQ for KV-cache events. vLLM workers publish raw KV events locally via ZMQ, and Dynamo normalizes and republishes them for routing decisions.
insights.so_what: Live KV-cache telemetry from engines is the foundation of precise cache-aware placement.
insights.quote: In Dynamo 1.4.2, the default AICR Kubernetes path uses TCP for requests and ZMQ for KV-cache events.
insights.locator: The request plane and KV-cache event
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: Dynamo can alternatively predict KV-cache state from where it sent requests, but prediction cannot see evictions. The router's view then drifts from what workers actually hold and routing quality degrades, especially under memory pressure, so the AICR configuration enables live events.
insights.so_what: Predicted-cache routing is a hidden performance risk, and live cache events should be preferred under load.
insights.quote: Prediction cannot see evictions, so the router’s view can drift from what each worker actually holds, and routing quality can degrade, especially under memory pressure.
insights.locator: Both paths use worker-published KV-cache events
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

themes.theme: Two routing paths: Dynamo Frontend vs Gateway API/EPP

insights.claim: In the default Dynamo Frontend router path (DYN_ROUTER_MODE=kv), the Frontend tokenizes each request, scores workers on prefix overlap and current load, and dispatches over TCP. It is the smallest topology, the most production-proven option, and needs no gateway or EPP components.
insights.so_what: Teams owning model-specific endpoints get the simplest, lowest-overhead route to production.
insights.quote: It is the smallest topology for deploying and validating a Dynamo graph and is the most production-proven serving option.
insights.locator: This path is suitable when an
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: In the GAIE/EPP path, agentgateway resolves an HTTPRoute to an InferencePool created by the Dynamo operator. The Dynamo EPP picks the endpoint using Dynamo's KV router, and the gateway forwards the request to a Frontend sidecar in direct mode. This suits platform teams that manage shared ingress with Gateway API timeouts, retries and fallback.
insights.so_what: Dynamo plugs into the Kubernetes-standard inference gateway, which eases adoption in shared platform clusters.
insights.quote: This path is suitable when the platform team manages shared Kubernetes ingress and needs to configure model endpoint worker selection, timeouts, retries, and fallback through Gateway API mechanisms.
insights.locator: This path is suitable when the
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: The choice between paths depends on whether the Gateway or the Dynamo Frontend should handle forwarding to workers, including timeouts, retries and fallback. Both can sit behind a Gateway API HTTPRoute and both use the same worker-published KV-cache state.
insights.so_what: Cache-aware routing quality is the same either way, and the decision is about ownership of transport.
insights.quote: The routing path depends on whether the Gateway or the Dynamo Frontend should handle the forwarding of requests to the workers, including timeouts, retries, and fallback management.
insights.locator: The routing path depends on whether
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: Starting with Dynamo 1.5, a native Rust EPP will replace the current Go EPP framework with Dynamo's Rust KV router embedded through CGO. It will implement GAIE's Lightweight Endpoint Picker interface directly and run the full router in-process, cutting per-request EPP overhead.
insights.so_what: The next Dynamo release should lower gateway-path latency, making the Kubernetes-native ingress option more competitive.
insights.quote: Starting with Dynamo 1.5, a native Rust EPP replaces the Go/CGO bridge.
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

themes.theme: AICR five-step deploy and validation flow

insights.claim: AICR separates runtime setup from application deployment: snapshot the cluster, generate a Dynamo inference recipe from the detected Kubernetes distribution, accelerator and OS, render a bundle, deploy it, and validate it before installing the application's DynamoGraphDeployment.
insights.so_what: A gated runtime validation step reduces failed production rollouts of GPU inference clusters.
insights.quote: AICR separates runtime setup from application deployment.
insights.locator: AICR separates runtime setup from application
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: AICR bundles can be deployed with Helmfile, which applies dependency tiers in order and independent components concurrently, or with a Helm deploy.sh fallback. For production it also renders GitOps bundles for Argo CD and Flux.
insights.so_what: Fitting into standard GitOps tooling lowers the adoption barrier for enterprise platform teams.
insights.quote: For production, AICR also renders GitOps bundles with --deployer argocd, --deployer argocd-helm, and --deployer flux.
insights.locator: For production, AICR also renders GitOps
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: Deployment and conformance validation check the cluster baseline (GPU allocatable capacity, a working nvidia-smi), GPU Operator and Dynamo health, DRA and secure accelerator access, gang scheduling and autoscaling, Prometheus metrics, and Gateway API readiness. Performance validation runs separately because it consumes the GPUs under test.
insights.so_what: Standardized conformance checks could become a de facto certification for AI-ready Kubernetes clusters.
insights.quote: Performance validation runs separately because it deploys a temporary serving workload and consumes the GPUs under test.
insights.locator: The application DynamoGraphDeployment is installed only
insights.speaker: Stefan Schimanski

insights.claim: AICR and Dynamo are open-source components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, with community resources on GitHub and Slack and a hands-on AICR workshop at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America.
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is courting the cloud-native community to make its stack the default for AI inference on Kubernetes.
insights.quote: NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) and NVIDIA Dynamo are open-source components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform.
